## TL;DR

A review registration could outlive its reviewer and then refuse every later "review again" until the server restarted. The fix covers the three leak paths and the refusal text. Reviews that fail to start release their registration. `review cancel` releases it even when the child is already gone. A registration with no live process is reaped once it outlives the review timeout, and the refusal now names the pid and start time. The scoped `repoos check --changed main` run was still in progress when this draft was written; the handoff result is not claimed here.

## Work and rationale

The reported symptom was "a review is already running for this task" with no reviewer process. Three separate holes can each produce it, and I closed all three.

1. **The runner never reaped review entries.** `AgentRunner.reconcileDeadAgents()` skips review turns, and reviews normally finish through the child's `close` event. An adopted review (re-attached after a reload) has no `close`, so when its process died the entry stayed in `entries` and `isRunning()` kept answering true. This change is committed on the branch: a dead review now goes through `cleanup`, which fires `onReviewDone` and writes a failed report.

2. **`ReviewManager.cancel()` left its own registration behind.** It set `run.cancelled`, stopped the child and cleared the timer, but left the `runs` entry in place. Its early return also skipped cleanup when no live child existed. In `src/server/review.ts`, `cancel()` now releases the `runs` entry and any completion fence unconditionally. A live child still finalizes as cancelled, because the durable cancelled marker is written first.

3. **Nothing expired a registration.** `Run` now carries `startedAt`, and each completion fence has a `completionSince` timestamp. `isRunning()` calls `reapStaleRegistration()` first. That reaper clears an entry only when it has no live runner process and has outlived `reviewTimeoutMs`, and it logs a warning when it does. A fresh entry with no process yet is left alone so the reaper cannot race a legitimate start. A live process is never reaped, however old. `runningCount()` reaps first too, so a stale entry cannot hold the idle check open.

The refusal now reads `a review is already running for this task (pid 4242, since 2026-11-10T17:27:00.000Z)`, or `no reviewer process id yet` when the registration has no process. The prefix is unchanged.

The spawn path also changed. `spawnDurable` used to let a throwing `runner.startReview` escape. It now becomes an ordinary failed start, which releases the registration. The completion fence release is identity-guarded, so a late finalize cannot delete a newer registration that the reaper already replaced.

Decisions:
- The stale threshold is the configured review timeout, as the spec asks, not a new constant.
- The reaper logs and clears but writes no task Activity marker. `isRunning()` runs on read paths and in the watchdog, and a task-file write there would be an unrequested side effect.
- `runner.startReview` also has its own "a review is already running for this task" refusal in `src/server/agents.ts` (around line 6942). It carries no pid or time. I left it alone because the review gate calls `runner.isRunning(key)` inside `registration()`, so the gate reports the live entry with its pid and time before this line is reached. It is a backstop, not the user-visible path.

Formatting: `bun run fmt` reformatted the two changed files, which were the only dirty paths before the run.

## Approaches tried

I considered a periodic reaper timer. I rejected it because every consumer already calls `isRunning()` on the path that matters, so a timer would add a second clock and a shutdown-ordering problem. I also considered only removing the runner's review skip. That fixes the adopted-review case but leaves the `cancel()` leak and the hung-finalize leak, so I kept all three fixes.

## Challenges and blockers

- The test file has a mock runner, and `spawnDurable`'s failure branch can write a marker through the runner. The mock needs a `system()` method, which the file already provides.
- I could not reproduce the production incident. The machine was offline and the reviewer ran into an API outage. The tests simulate the leaked state directly: a registration with no process, a spawn that throws, and an entry that outlives the timeout. I did not observe the real outage path end to end. A human should confirm with a live `review again` after deploy.
- Only the nine tests in `src/ui-app/tests/review-stale-registration.test.ts` were run in this session, and all passed. `review-completion.test.ts` already matches the refusal by prefix.

## Key learnings

Every holder of an in-memory registration needs a release path that does not depend on the child's exit event. That event never arrives for a process re-attached after a reload. A `cancel` that returns early when the child is already gone is also a leak: cancel has to release bookkeeping whether or not anything is left to kill. Putting the reaper inside `isRunning()` means every caller gets the staleness check without each one implementing its own.
